paragraphs.source_en: I love on the back cover how it has this great little pitch that says, “The only book used in both grade school and graduate school.” It’s true. It’s all simple physics puzzles that can be explained to a twelve-year-old child and can be explained to a twenty-five-yearold grad student in physics. They all have fundamental insights in physics. They’re all kind of tricky, but anyone can get to the answer through purely logical reasoning. [4] The Lessons of History by Will and Ariel Durant This is a great book I really like that summarizes some of the larger themes of history; it’s very incisive. And unlike most history books, it’s actually really small, and it covers a lot of ground. [7] The Sovereign Individual: Mastering the Transition to the Information Age by James Dale Davidson and Lord William Rees- Mogg This is the best book I’ve read since Sapiens (far less mainstream, though).
